text:
maya: Heads-up — the new NextKit sample (edge runtime + LangChain bridge) is failing our eval harness intermittently. Repro steps below.

omar: Ugh, saw that earlier. Is it the auth refresh loop or the streaming socket?

maya: Looks like auth + retry. In browser dev mode the embed request sometimes gets a 401 then our SDK retries but with an expired token. Eval harness sees truncated outputs.

paul_dev: Can you paste the fetch snippet from the sample app? I want to check header wiring.

maya: Sure:```js
const res = await fetch('/api/generate', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: {
    'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY}`
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({ prompt })
});
```

rachel: That env var is only available server-side. Are we accidentally running parts of the handler in edge/edge-compat that expects browser-like env?

samir: The NextKit starter sets `runtime: 'edge'` on the api route for perf. Edge env doesn't have process.env the same way in Vercel. We added a fallback that reads from a top-level wrapper but maybe our local dev overlay is inconsistent.

maya: The confusing bit is the SDK parity: the same code path in node-runtime returns a 200, edge returns 401 during token refresh window. SDK v0.12.3 had a fix but next-starter pinned to 0.12.1.

omar: So two issues: starter pins old SDK, and runtime mismatch for env access. We should either default `runtime: nodejs` in starter or update SDK. Which is less friction for users?

paul_dev: Update SDK in the starter, add a runtime note in README. Also add a small guard in the api route that throws a clear error if Authorization is missing. Eg:```js
if (!process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY) {
  throw new Error('REDWOOD_API_KEY missing — make sure to set it in your .env.local or use server runtime')
}
```

rachel: Agree. Also add a quickline in the eval harness to retry with exponential backoff on 401 only after refreshing token. Right now the harness treats any non-200 as immediate failure.

samir: I'll raise a tiny PR for starter: bump SDK to 0.12.3, add README section "Edge runtime gotchas", and add the env-guard.

maya: Thanks. For tracking: tag the failing CI job as flaky with a link to the harness run: https://ci.internal/runs/8342 (shows truncated output).

devex-bot: Created issue #1482: "nextkit-starter: auth refresh + edge runtime causes intermittent 401 in eval harness" assigned to samir — https://issues.redwood/1482

omar: One more ask — can we add a tiny integration test that spins up the sample in edge mode locally and triggers a simulated token expiry? Minimal, but it would have caught this.

paul_dev: Yep — use msw to mock the token endpoint and force a 401, assert the SDK refresh path is used. I'll sketch it.

maya: Cool. Leaving notes in the starter repo README under "Known DX friction" so new users don't get stuck.

rachel: Nice catch. Once PR lands, I'll re-run the eval harness and mark the job non-flaky. :rocket:
